title: Redshift and EMR: warehousing and big data

kcs.statement: Amazon Redshift is a petabyte-scale, columnar data warehouse for fast SQL analytics on large volumes of structured data.
Amazon EMR runs managed big data frameworks such as Apache Spark, Hadoop and Hive on clusters of EC2 instances (or serverless) to process very large datasets.
RDS and Aurora serve transactional (OLTP) workloads with many small reads and writes; Redshift serves analytical (OLAP) queries that aggregate large historical datasets.

problem_ideas: A retailer wants daily sales reports over 5 years of transactions from many systems: RDS or Redshift?
A data science team already has Spark jobs on-prem and wants a managed cluster: which service?
